title: Mac Dictation Not Working? Fixes for macOS 27 That Actually Work
why: Apple's macOS 27 guide: turn Dictation on in Keyboard settings; when Voice Control is on, standard Dictation isn't available. Troubleshooting angle for a high-frustration query. Lazur fit: a fallback voice layer.

title: Enhanced Dictation on Mac: Which Macs and Languages Qualify
why: Apple says enhanced dictation needs M3 or later with at least 12GB unified memory and is English only. Older Macs won't get it. Caveat: the guide doesn't say whether basic dictation works offline.

title: Voice Control vs Dictation on Mac: Why Only One Can Run
why: Apple's dictation guide states that when Voice Control is on, standard macOS Dictation isn't available. Readers searching this are confused about which one to use and when. Explains the switch with Apple's wording.

title: What Changed in Mac Dictation With macOS 27 Golden Gate
why: Apple's dictation guide covers macOS 27 and says Apple Intelligence uses an on-device model to improve spelling, punctuation and capitalization. Pairs with enhanced-dictation requirements. Caveat: the guide doesn't say whether basic dictation works offline.

title: Should You Share Dictation Audio With Apple? The Setting Explained
why: Apple asks when you enable Dictation whether to share audio recordings to improve Siri and Dictation; you can change it later under Privacy & Security. Apple also says some voice input is processed on-device. Good privacy-decision explainer.

title: Dictation Errors vs Typing Errors: What the Lab Data Shows
why: Ruan et al. (arXiv 2016): corrected error rate 5.30% for speech vs 11.22% for keyboard; uncorrected 1.30% vs 0.79%. Speech wins on corrected errors but leaves more uncorrected ones. Caveat: phone lab study, not desktop Mac typing.

title: Voice Typing for RSI: What It Can and Can't Fix
why: NIOSH lists high repetition plus forceful hand/wrist exertion as a combined risk for hand/wrist tendinitis. Voice typing cuts keystroke repetition but not posture or mouse use. Caveat: not medical advice; no dictation-and-RSI study found yet.

title: How Common Is Work-Related Carpal Tunnel? The 2015 Numbers
targetKeyword: work related carpal tunnel syndrome how common
why: NIOSH Worker Health Chart (2015 NHIS): about 2,445,000 US workers had current carpal tunnel attributed to work, unadjusted prevalence 1.68% (95% CI 1.46-1.92). Caveat: 2015 data; a 2010 analysis reported a higher work-attributed count.

title: Screen Recording Permission on Mac: What to Allow for an AI Assistant
why: Apple: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording, toggled per app. Apple warns that data from third-party apps is governed by their own privacy policies. Caveat: Apple's page doesn't say what happens when the permission is off.

title: Screen Recording Permission Keeps Resetting on Mac? Here's Why
targetKeyword: screen recording permission keeps resetting mac
why: Third-party guide: an app must restart after permission is granted, Sequoia shows monthly re-authorization prompts, and tccutil reset ScreenCapture clears stale entries. Caveat: Apple's pages didn't confirm the monthly prompt; verify on a Sequoia Mac.

title: Where Your Screenshots Go When AI Watches Your Mac
why: Per TNW (Apr 20, 2026): OpenAI's Codex Chronicle sends screenshots to OpenAI servers for OCR and analysis, deletes raw captures after six hours, and keeps text summaries as plain text on your Mac. Not offered in EU, UK or Switzerland.

title: ChatGPT Voice on Mac: Can It See Your Screen?
why: TechCrunch (Jul 24, 2026): new ChatGPT Voice on Mac lets you talk to control agents and tasks; screen access comes via Appshots, which include alt-text. Article doesn't confirm continuous screen watching or which plan is required.

title: Claude Desktop Voice on Mac: Dictation First, Not a Voice Chat
why: Claude's Mac help: Caps Lock starts real-time dictation into the prompt (off by default; needs macOS 14+ and Speech recognition permission). The article doesn't describe spoken replies. Page only says 'Updated this week'.

title: Voice In, Voice Out: Which Mac AI Tools Actually Talk Back
targetKeyword: mac AI assistant that talks back
why: Claude's documented Mac voice input transcribes into the prompt rather than replying aloud; ChatGPT's July 2026 desktop voice is agent-focused. Sources conflict on spoken replies, so test each product before recommending. Lazur answers out loud.

title: Mac Notch Apps: What Each One Is Actually For
why: Roundups group notch apps into productivity (NotchNook, Brow), media (Boring Notch, Alcove), notch hiding (TopNotch) and menu bar management (Bartender). Sources are vendor-written and subjective; check each app's current site. Not opened directly.

why: Apple's shortcuts reference lists core keys such as Command-Z, Command-F, Command-S, Command-P and Command-T. Start with a short list instead of memorizing everything. Voice covers text entry, not most navigation.

title: What Is a Good Typing Speed on a Mac? Benchmarks That Hold Up
why: Aalto CHI 2018 study (168,000 volunteers): about 52 WPM average on computer keyboards. Caveat: self-selected online sample; the PDF was unreadable in my fetch, so the figure comes from secondary sites. Verify before publishing.

why: App-specific long tail: people searching for a single pro app want a path to a first project. Angle: ask about the screen you're on instead of watching a course. No search-volume or survey data gathered yet.

why: Input quality affects dictation accuracy. A third-party guide says you can choose the mic in the Dictation Microphone source menu; Apple's page I opened didn't confirm this. Verify on a Mac before publishing.

title: Accessibility vs Screen Recording: Two Permissions Your AI Assistant Asks For
why: Vendor blog (Fazm): screen capture needs Screen Recording, while reading UI elements needs Accessibility. Apple's screen-recording page I opened doesn't cover Accessibility. Single vendor source; verify in System Settings.

title: Siri AI on Mac: What Shift-Command-6 Does With Your Screen
why: Apple's shortcut page: in macOS 27 with Siri AI (Beta) on, Shift-Command-6 asks Siri about the selected area. Beta feature, so availability may change. Compare with third-party screen assistants.

title: Claude Desktop Quick Entry on Mac: Screenshots, Windows, and Voice
why: Claude's Mac help: double-tap Option opens quick entry, which shares screenshots and app windows; Caps Lock dictation is a separate feature. Useful comparison for a screen-aware workflow. Page dated only 'Updated this week'.

title: Google Docs Voice Typing on Mac: Setup, Browsers and What Works
why: Google's page lists Chrome, Edge and Safari, English-only voice commands, and no Mac shortcut (some blogs cite ⌘+Shift+S, unconfirmed). Apple dictation works in any typeable field as a fallback. Demand not measured. Natural Lazur mention: one voice tool across apps.

title: Dictate in Microsoft Word on Mac: Option-F1, Microsoft 365 Limits and Commands
why: Microsoft: Dictate is for Microsoft 365 subscribers only, needs a reliable internet connection, starts with Option+F1 from Home > Dictate, and lists English punctuation commands. Demand not measured. Lazur as a fallback for non-subscribers.

title: Make Your Mac Read Text Out Loud: Speak Selection, Option-Esc and Controls
targetKeyword: make mac read text out loud
why: Apple: System Settings > Accessibility > Read & Speak > Speak selection; default shortcut Option-Esc; with no selection it reads readable items in the window; the controller adjusts speed and skips sentences. Demand not measured. Lazur natural mention as a contrast to speech-out assistants.

title: Mac Dictation Punctuation Commands: Apple's Built-In List Explained
why: Apple's built-in commands ('new paragraph', 'open parenthesis', 'no space on', 'caps on') work with no setup. Turning Voice Control on replaces standard Dictation. Demand not measured. Distinguish from Intent Mode commands, which finish tasks rather than format text.

title: Dictation for Non-Native English Speakers on Mac: What Accuracy Data Shows
targetKeyword: dictation for non-native English speakers mac
why: 2025 arXiv (non-native speakers): mean MER 0.054 (Whisper) and 0.056 (AssemblyAI) on read speech; RevAI 0.063 on spontaneous speech. Caveat: MER, not WER; the abstract has no native baseline or per-language rates, so check the full paper.

title: Dictation in a Noisy Office on Mac: What Error Rates Look Like
why: Kili (2026), citing Szymański et al. 2020: real call-centre WER 16.5–19.2% vs 10.2–11.6% on Switchboard. At 0 dB SNR, AMI reached 25.43%. Secondary source; no Mac dictation test in offices found. Demand not measured.

title: Voice Writing for Dyslexia and ADHD on Mac: What Research Does and Doesn't Show
targetKeyword: dictation for ADHD and dyslexia mac
why: 2023 Frontiers editorial: speech-to-text tested in one child study (ages 10–13, n=12+16) with no results reported; the adult dyslexia study used keyboarding; ADHD not covered. Vendor claims of big gains are unverified. Thin evidence, so frame it as what is unproven.

title: AI That Describes Your Mac Screen for Low Vision: What Apple Offers
targetKeyword: AI describe mac screen low vision

targetKeyword: control mac without hands voice control
why: Apple: Voice Control has Command and Dictation modes, 'Show numbers' and 'Show grid' overlays, Stop/Start listening, and replaces standard Dictation while on. Apple does not frame it for limited mobility, and no usage numbers were found. Differentiate from RSI pain posts.

title: Dictate Into Apple Notes on Mac for Quick Capture
why: Apple: Dictation works anywhere you can type; start with the Microphone key or a shortcut set in Keyboard > Dictation; check the 'processed on your device' setting. Quick-capture angle. Demand not measured. Natural Lazur mention only if it captures notes.

why: Apple: dictation stops automatically if no speech is detected for 30 seconds, and there is no length timeout. This covers pausing to think rather than setup failures. Demand not measured. Natural Lazur angle: a voice tool that keeps your thought.
